Compliance · EU

Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation

Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 · applies since 2024-12-30 · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Crypto-asset service providers authorised under MiCA (Art. 68), and issuers of crypto-assets for other titles.

A check shows a breach in code; it does not certify that a point is met. List scraped from the publisher's document on 2026-11-01. A point here means: Article, numbered paragraph and lettered or roman point at every depth; Annex, its Parts, Sections and Chapters, and its numbered points. Recitals, footnotes, amendment markers and correlation tables left out (consolidated text 02023R1114-20240109).

Art. 1 Subject matter
Art. 1(1) Sets uniform rules for public offers and trading admission of crypto-assets, plus service providers. Coming soon
Art. 1(2) Introduces the list of specific matters the Regulation covers.
Art. 1(2)(a) Covers transparency and disclosure duties for issuing, offering and admitting crypto-assets to trading. Coming soon
Art. 1(2)(b) Covers authorisation, supervision, operation, organisation and governance of providers and token issuers. Coming soon
Art. 1(2)(c) Covers protection of crypto-asset holders during issuance, public offer and trading admission. Coming soon
Art. 1(2)(d) Covers protection of clients of crypto-asset service providers. Coming soon
Art. 1(2)(e) Covers measures against insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation to keep markets sound. Coming soon
Art. 2 Scope
Art. 2(1) Regulation applies to persons issuing, offering, listing or servicing crypto-assets in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 2(2) Introduces the list of persons excluded from the Regulation.
Art. 2(2)(a) Excludes those serving only their parent or sister or subsidiary companies. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(b) Excludes insolvency liquidators and administrators, apart from one article. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(c) Excludes the ECB, national central banks acting as monetary authorities, and public authorities. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(d) Excludes the European Investment Bank and its subsidiaries. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(e) Excludes the EFSF and the European Stability Mechanism. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(f) Excludes public international organisations. Coming soon
Art. 2(3) Excludes crypto-assets that are unique and non-fungible. Coming soon
Art. 2(4) Introduces the list of asset types excluded from the Regulation.
Art. 2(4)(a) Excludes crypto-assets that qualify as financial instruments. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(b) Excludes crypto-assets that are deposits, including structured ones. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(c) Excludes funds, unless they are e-money tokens. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(d) Excludes securitisation positions as defined in the securitisation regulation. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(e) Excludes insurance and reinsurance products under the Solvency directive classes. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(f) Excludes pension products mainly meant to provide retirement income. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(g) Excludes officially recognised occupational pension schemes under the cited directives. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(h) Excludes employer-funded individual pension products where no choice of product or provider exists. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(i) Excludes the pan-European Personal Pension Product. Coming soon
Art. 2(4)(j) Excludes social security schemes covered by the two named regulations. Coming soon
Art. 2(5) ESMA must issue guidelines on classifying crypto-assets as financial instruments by end of 2024. Coming soon
Art. 2(6) Regulation does not affect the single supervisory mechanism regulation. Coming soon
Art. 3 Definitions
Art. 3(1) Introduces the definitions used in the Regulation.
Art. 3(1)(1) Defines distributed ledger technology. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(2) Defines a distributed ledger as a shared, synchronised transaction record. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(3) Defines consensus mechanism as the rules for validating transactions across nodes. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(4) Defines a DLT network node. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(5) Defines crypto-asset as a transferable digital representation of value or rights. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(6) Defines asset-referenced token as a stable-value crypto-asset referencing other values or rights. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(7) Defines e-money token as a crypto-asset tracking a single official currency. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(8) Defines official currency as one issued by a central bank or monetary authority. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(9) Defines utility token as one giving access only to issuer's goods or services. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(10) Defines issuer of crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(11) Defines applicant issuer of asset-referenced or e-money tokens seeking authorisation or trading. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(12) Defines offer to the public as a communication giving enough information to decide on purchase. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(13) Defines offeror of crypto-assets to the public. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(14) Defines funds by reference to the payment services directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(15) Defines crypto-asset service provider as an authorised professional provider of crypto-asset services. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16) Introduces the list of defined crypto-asset services.
Art. 3(1)(16)(a) Lists custody and administration on behalf of clients as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(b) Lists operating a crypto-asset trading platform as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(c) Lists exchanging crypto-assets for funds as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(d) Lists exchanging crypto-assets for other crypto-assets as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(e) Lists executing client orders for crypto-assets as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(f) Lists placing of crypto-assets as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(g) Lists receiving and transmitting client orders as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(h) Lists advice on crypto-assets as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(i) Lists crypto-asset portfolio management as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(16)(j) Lists transfer services for crypto-assets on behalf of clients as a service. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(17) Defines custody as safekeeping or controlling client crypto-assets or access keys. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(18) Defines operating a trading platform as running multilateral matching systems. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(19) Defines exchange of crypto-assets for funds using own capital. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(20) Defines exchange of crypto-assets for other crypto-assets using own capital. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(21) Defines executing client orders to buy, sell or subscribe to crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(22) Defines placing as marketing crypto-assets for the offeror or related party. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(23) Defines receiving orders and passing them to a third party for execution. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(24) Defines advice as personalised recommendations on crypto-asset transactions or services. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(25) Defines portfolio management as discretionary management of client portfolios holding crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(26) Defines transfer services as moving crypto-assets between ledger addresses for others. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(27) Defines management body of an issuer, offeror or service provider. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(28) Defines credit institution by reference to EU banking law. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(29) Defines investment firm by reference to EU capital requirements and MiFID. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(30) Defines qualified investors by reference to MiFID II annex. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(31) Defines close links by reference to MiFID II. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(32) Defines reserve of assets as the basket securing claims against the issuer. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33) Introduces the definition of home Member State.
Art. 3(1)(33)(a) Home state for an EU-registered offeror is where its registered office is. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33)(b) Offeror without EU office but with branches chooses among branch Member States. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33)(c) Third-country offeror without EU branch: first offer state or first admission application state. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33)(d) For asset-referenced token issuers, home state is where the registered office is. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33)(e) For e-money token issuers, home state is where authorised as bank or e-money institution. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(33)(f) For service providers, home state is where the registered office is. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(34) Defines host Member State as the non-home state where offers or services occur. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(35) Introduces the definition of competent authority.
Art. 3(1)(35)(a) Authority designated under Article 93 for offerors, ART issuers and service providers. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(35)(b) Authority designated under the e-money directive for e-money token issuers. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(36) Defines qualifying holding as at least 10% capital or votes, or significant influence. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(37) Defines retail holder as a natural person acting outside trade or profession. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(38) Defines online interface as software giving holders or clients access to assets or services. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(39) Defines client as anyone receiving crypto-asset services from a provider. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(40) Defines matched principal trading by reference to MiFID II. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(41) Defines payment services by reference to the payment services directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(42) Defines payment service provider by reference to the payment services directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(43) Defines electronic money institution by reference to the e-money directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(44) Defines electronic money by reference to the e-money directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(45) Defines personal data by reference to the GDPR. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(46) Defines payment institution by reference to the payment services directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(47) Defines UCITS management company by reference to the UCITS directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(48) Defines alternative investment fund manager by reference to the AIFM directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(49) Defines financial instrument by reference to MiFID II. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(50) Defines deposit by reference to the deposit guarantee directive. Coming soon
Art. 3(1)(51) Defines structured deposit by reference to MiFID II. Coming soon
Art. 3(2) Commission may adopt delegated acts refining and updating the definitions. Coming soon
Art. 4 Offers to the public of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens
Art. 4(1) Public offers of other crypto-assets in the Union need the listed preconditions met.
Art. 4(1)(a) Offeror must be a legal person. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(b) Offeror must have prepared a compliant crypto-asset white paper. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(c) Offeror must have notified the white paper to the authority. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(d) Offeror must have published the white paper as required. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(e) Any marketing communications must be drafted in line with Article 7. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(f) Any marketing communications must be published in line with Article 9. Coming soon
Art. 4(1)(g) Offeror must comply with the offeror requirements in Article 14. Coming soon
Art. 4(2) Exempts certain small or restricted offers from white paper notification and publication duties.
Art. 4(2)(a) Exempts offers to fewer than 150 persons per Member State acting on own account. Coming soon
Art. 4(2)(b) Exempts offers totalling up to one million euro over twelve months. Coming soon
Art. 4(2)(c) Exempts offers made only to qualified investors who alone can hold the asset. Coming soon
Art. 4(3) Title does not apply to free, mining-reward, existing-service utility or limited-network offers, with notification rules.
Art. 4(3)(a) Exempts crypto-assets offered for free. Coming soon
Art. 4(3)(b) Exempts crypto-assets automatically created as rewards for ledger maintenance or validation. Coming soon
Art. 4(3)(c) Exempts utility tokens giving access to an existing, operating good or service. Coming soon
Art. 4(3)(d) Exempts tokens usable only within a limited merchant network contracted with the offeror. Coming soon
Art. 4(4) Exemptions are lost if the offeror signals intent to seek trading admission. Coming soon
Art. 4(5) Custody and transfer of exempt-offer assets needs no authorisation, unless exceptions apply.
Art. 4(5)(a) Exception: another non-exempt public offer of the same crypto-asset exists. Coming soon
Art. 4(5)(b) Exemption from white paper duty applies where the crypto-asset is already admitted to a trading platform. Coming soon
Art. 4(6) Offers of utility tokens for not-yet-existing services may run at most twelve months from white paper publication. Coming soon
Art. 4(7) Later offers count as separate offers; no new white paper needed if original published and author consents. Coming soon
Art. 4(8) A voluntarily drawn-up white paper in an exempt offer still falls under this Title's rules. Coming soon
Art. 5 Admission to trading of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens
Art. 5(1) Anyone seeking trading admission of such crypto-assets must satisfy listed conditions first.
Art. 5(1)(a) Person seeking admission to trading must be a legal person. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(b) A white paper must be drawn up under Article 6. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(c) The white paper must be notified to the authority under Article 8. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(d) The white paper must be published as Article 9 requires. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(e) Any marketing communications must be drafted in line with Article 7. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(f) Any marketing communications must be published as Article 9 requires. Coming soon
Art. 5(1)(g) Must comply with the conduct obligations of Article 14. Coming soon
Art. 5(2) Platform operator admitting an asset on its own initiative without a required white paper takes on those duties. Coming soon
Art. 5(3) Applicant and platform operator may agree in writing that the operator handles some listed duties. Coming soon
Art. 5(4) Certain white paper requirements are disapplied in the circumstances listed below.
Art. 5(4)(a) Asset is already admitted on another Union crypto-asset trading platform. Coming soon
Art. 5(4)(b) White paper complies, is kept updated, and its author consents in writing to reuse. Coming soon
Art. 6 Content and form of the crypto-asset white paper
Art. 6(1) White paper must contain the Annex I information, and identify the drafter if a third party.
Art. 6(1)(a) White paper must include information about the offeror or person seeking admission. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(b) White paper must include issuer information where the issuer differs from offeror. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(c) White paper must include platform operator information when the operator drafts it. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(d) White paper must describe the crypto-asset project. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(e) White paper must describe the public offer or admission to trading. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(f) White paper must describe the crypto-asset. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(g) White paper must state rights and obligations attached to the asset. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(h) White paper must describe the underlying technology. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(i) White paper must set out the risks. Coming soon
Art. 6(1)(j) White paper must disclose climate and environmental impacts of the consensus mechanism. Coming soon
Art. 6(2) White paper information must be fair, clear, non-misleading, concise, and without material omissions. Coming soon
Art. 6(3) First page must carry the prescribed statement that no authority approved the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 6(4) White paper must not make claims about the asset's future value. Coming soon
Art. 6(5) White paper must include clear statements of specified risks.
Art. 6(5)(a) State that the asset may lose value partly or wholly. Coming soon
Art. 6(5)(b) State that the asset may not always be transferable. Coming soon
Art. 6(5)(c) State that the asset may be illiquid. Coming soon
Art. 6(5)(d) For utility tokens, state they may not be exchangeable for promised goods or services. Coming soon
Art. 6(5)(e) State the asset is not covered by investor compensation schemes. Coming soon
Art. 6(5)(f) State the asset is not covered by deposit guarantee schemes. Coming soon
Art. 6(6) White paper needs a management body statement confirming compliance and accuracy of its content. Coming soon
Art. 6(7) White paper must include a plain-language summary with a specified warning.
Art. 6(7)(a) Summary warns it should be read as an introduction to the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 6(7)(b) Summary warns purchase decisions should rely on the whole white paper. Coming soon
Art. 6(7)(c) Summary warns the offer is not a solicitation to buy financial instruments. Coming soon
Art. 6(7)(d) Summary warns the white paper is not a prospectus or other offer document. Coming soon
Art. 6(8) White paper must show its notification date and a table of contents. Coming soon
Art. 6(9) White paper must be written in an official or customary international finance language of relevant states. Coming soon
Art. 6(10) White paper must be made available in machine-readable format. Coming soon
Art. 6(11) ESMA must draft technical standards on forms and templates for machine-readable white papers. Coming soon
Art. 6(12) ESMA must draft standards on presenting sustainability indicators for environmental impacts. Coming soon
Art. 7 Marketing communications
Art. 7(1) Marketing communications must meet listed requirements, adjusting wording for the issuing party.
Art. 7(1)(a) Marketing communications must be clearly identifiable as such. Coming soon
Art. 7(1)(b) Marketing information must be fair, clear and not misleading. Coming soon
Art. 7(1)(c) Marketing information must be consistent with the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 7(1)(d) Marketing must state a white paper exists and give website, phone and email contacts. Coming soon
Art. 7(1)(e) Marketing must carry the prescribed statement that no authority reviewed or approved it. Coming soon
Art. 7(2) No marketing may be disseminated before the required white paper is published. Coming soon
Art. 7(3) Host-state authority may assess marketing compliance; home-state authority assists on consistency. Coming soon
Art. 7(4) Host-state authority must promptly notify home-state authority when using supervisory powers. Coming soon
Art. 8 Notification of the crypto-asset white paper and of the marketing communications
Art. 8(1) White paper must be notified to the home Member State authority. Coming soon
Art. 8(2) Marketing communications must be notified to authorities on request. Coming soon
Art. 8(3) Authorities may not demand prior approval of white papers or marketing. Coming soon
Art. 8(4) Notification must explain why the asset is not excluded, e-money or asset-referenced.
Art. 8(4)(a) Explain why the asset is not excluded from scope under Article 2(4). Coming soon
Art. 8(4)(b) Explain why the asset is not an e-money token. Coming soon
Art. 8(4)(c) Explain why the asset is not an asset-referenced token. Coming soon
Art. 8(5) Notification must occur at least 20 working days before publication. Coming soon
Art. 8(6) Notification must list host states and start date; authority informs host contact points. Coming soon
Art. 8(7) Home authority forwards notification information to ESMA, which registers the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 9 Publication of the crypto-asset white paper and of the marketing communications
Art. 9(1) White papers and marketing must be published on a public website before offer starts and kept available. Coming soon
Art. 9(2) Published documents must be identical to the notified or modified versions. Coming soon
Art. 10 Result of the offer to the public and safeguarding arrangements
Art. 10(1) Time-limited offerors must publish the offer result within 20 working days of subscription end. Coming soon
Art. 10(2) Open-ended offerors must publish units in circulation at least monthly. Coming soon
Art. 10(3) Time-limited offerors must safeguard funds raised, held in custody by specified institutions.
Art. 10(3)(a) Raised funds may be held by a credit institution. Coming soon
Art. 10(3)(b) Raised crypto-assets may be held by a custody-providing crypto-asset service provider. Coming soon
Art. 10(4) Open-ended offers must keep safeguarding until the withdrawal right expires. Coming soon
Art. 11 Rights of offerors and persons seeking admission to trading of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens
Art. 11(1) After publication, offerors may offer assets Union-wide and have them admitted to trading. Coming soon
Art. 11(2) Publishers of compliant white papers face no further information requirements for the offer. Coming soon
Art. 12 Modification of published crypto-asset white papers and of published marketing communications
Art. 12(1) Published white papers and marketing must be modified on significant new factors or material errors. Coming soon
Art. 12(2) Modified documents must be notified with reasons at least seven working days before publication. Coming soon
Art. 12(3) On publication, inform the public on website of the modification and summarise reasons. Coming soon
Art. 12(4) Modified documents must keep the same order of information as the originals. Coming soon
Art. 12(5) Home authority forwards modified documents to host authorities and ESMA within five working days. Coming soon
Art. 12(6) Modified documents and reasons must be published on the website under Article 9. Coming soon
Art. 12(7) Modified documents must be time-stamped, latest marked applicable, and all kept available. Coming soon
Art. 12(8) Modifications to utility token white papers cannot extend the twelve-month limit. Coming soon
Art. 12(9) Older versions stay online ten years with an invalid warning and link to current version. Coming soon
Art. 13 Right of withdrawal
Art. 13(1) Retail buyers get a 14-day no-cost, no-reason right to withdraw from purchases. Coming soon
Art. 13(2) Payments must be refunded within 14 days of withdrawal notice, using original payment means. Coming soon
Art. 13(3) White paper must give information on the right of withdrawal. Coming soon
Art. 13(4) No withdrawal right if assets were already admitted to trading before purchase. Coming soon
Art. 13(5) For time-limited offers, withdrawal cannot be exercised after the subscription period ends. Coming soon
Art. 14 Obligations of offerors and persons seeking admission to trading of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens
Art. 14(1) Offerors and applicants must meet conduct and security duties; ESMA issues guidelines on standards.
Art. 14(1)(a) Act honestly, fairly and professionally. Coming soon
Art. 14(1)(b) Communicate with holders and prospects fairly, clearly and without misleading. Coming soon
Art. 14(1)(c) Identify, prevent, manage and disclose conflicts of interest. Coming soon
Art. 14(1)(d) Keep systems and security access protocols in line with appropriate Union standards. Coming soon
Art. 14(2) Act in holders' best interests and treat them equally unless preferences are disclosed. Coming soon
Art. 14(3) Funds must be returned within 25 calendar days after an offer is cancelled. Coming soon
Art. 15 Liability for the information given in a crypto-asset white paper
Art. 15(1) Offerors and management are liable to holders for losses from misleading white paper information. Coming soon
Art. 15(2) Contractual exclusions or limits of this liability have no legal effect. Coming soon
Art. 15(3) Applicant is also responsible for misleading information supplied to the platform operator drafting the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 15(4) Holder must prove the infringement and that reliance affected their decision. Coming soon
Art. 15(5) No liability for reliance on the summary, except in specified cases.
Art. 15(5)(a) Summary is misleading, inaccurate or inconsistent with the rest of the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 15(5)(b) Summary lacks key information when read with the rest of the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 15(6) Article leaves other national civil liability untouched; introduces asset-referenced token title. Coming soon
Art. 16 Authorisation
Art. 16(1) Only authorised issuers or credit institutions may offer asset-referenced tokens; others need issuer consent.
Art. 16(1)(a) Issuer is an authorised Union-established legal person or undertaking. Coming soon
Art. 16(1)(b) Issuer is a credit institution complying with Article 17. Coming soon
Art. 16(2) Exempt issuers must still draw up and notify a white paper.
Art. 16(2)(a) Exemption where average outstanding value stays under five million euro and issuer unlinked. Coming soon
Art. 16(2)(b) Exemption where offer is solely to qualified investors who alone can hold it. Coming soon
Art. 16(3) Authorisation is valid Union-wide for offering or seeking trading of the token. Coming soon
Art. 16(4) Approved white papers and modified versions are valid across every EU member state. Coming soon
Art. 17 Requirements for credit institutions
Art. 17(1) Credit institutions may offer asset-referenced tokens publicly if they meet listed conditions.
Art. 17(1)(a) Credit institution must prepare a white paper and obtain home authority's approval. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b) Credit institution notifies authority at least 90 working days before first issuance, with specified documents.
Art. 17(1)(b)(i) Notification includes a programme of operations describing the intended business model. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(ii) Notification includes legal opinion that token is neither excluded crypto-asset nor e-money token. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(iii) Notification includes detailed description of governance arrangements. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(iv) Notification includes the policies and procedures required under the governance article. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(v) Notification describes contractual arrangements with third-party entities. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(vi) Notification describes the institution's business continuity policy. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(vii) Notification describes internal controls and risk management procedures. Coming soon
Art. 17(1)(b)(viii) Notification describes systems protecting data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality. Coming soon
Art. 17(2) Repeat notifiers may omit identical earlier information but must confirm it remains current. Coming soon
Art. 17(3) Authority checks notification completeness within 20 days; incomplete notification blocks public offering. Coming soon
Art. 17(4) Credit institutions issuing these tokens are exempt from several listed articles. Coming soon
Art. 17(5) Authority forwards information to central banks, which opine; negative opinion bars offering. Coming soon
Art. 17(6) Authority passes register information to ESMA, which publishes it by offer start. Coming soon
Art. 17(7) Authority tells ESMA of authorisation withdrawal within two working days; ESMA registers it. Coming soon
Art. 17(8) EBA drafts technical standards on white paper approval procedure by June 2024. Coming soon
Art. 18 Application for authorisation

Art. 18(2)(i) Application proves managers' good repute, knowledge, skills and experience. Coming soon
Art. 18(2)(j) Application proves qualifying shareholders are of good repute. Coming soon

Art. 18(2)(o) Application describes internal control and risk management procedures. Coming soon
Art. 18(2)(p) Application describes data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality safeguards. Coming soon

Art. 18(5)(b) Proof managers collectively have suitable competence and will commit sufficient time. Coming soon
Art. 18(5)(c) Proof qualifying shareholders have no relevant criminal convictions or penalties. Coming soon

Art. 19 Content and form of the crypto-asset white paper for asset-referenced tokens
Art. 19(1) Token white paper must contain specified information categories and identify any non-issuer offeror or author.
Art. 19(1)(a) White paper covers information about the issuer. Coming soon
Art. 19(1)(b) White paper covers information about the token. Coming soon

Art. 19(1)(d) White paper covers rights and obligations attached to the token. Coming soon

Art. 19(1)(g) White paper covers the reserve of assets. Coming soon

Art. 19(2) White paper information must be fair, clear, not misleading, concise and complete. Coming soon
Art. 19(3) White paper may not make claims about future token value beyond required statement. Coming soon
Art. 19(4) White paper must carry clear statements on specified token risks.
Art. 19(4)(a) Statement that token may lose value partly or wholly. Coming soon
Art. 19(4)(b) Statement that token may not always be transferable. Coming soon
Art. 19(4)(c) Statement that token may lack liquidity. Coming soon
Art. 19(4)(d) Statement that investor compensation schemes do not cover the token. Coming soon
Art. 19(4)(e) Statement that deposit guarantee schemes do not cover the token. Coming soon
Art. 19(5) White paper includes management body statement confirming compliance and accuracy. Coming soon
Art. 19(6) White paper includes plain-language summary with warnings and redemption right statement.
Art. 19(6)(a) Summary warns it should be read as an introduction. Coming soon
Art. 19(6)(b) Summary warns decisions should rest on the whole document. Coming soon
Art. 19(6)(c) Summary warns the offer is not a solicitation to buy financial instruments. Coming soon
Art. 19(6)(d) Summary warns the white paper is not a prospectus or offer document. Coming soon
Art. 19(7) White paper shows its notification date and a table of contents. Coming soon

Art. 20 Assessment of the application for authorisation
Art. 20(1) Authority checks application completeness within 25 working days and notifies applicant of gaps. Coming soon
Art. 20(2) Authority has 60 working days to assess compliance and draft a decision. Coming soon
Art. 20(3) Assessment clock pauses for missing information requests, up to 20 working days. Coming soon
Art. 20(4) Authority sends draft decision and application to EBA, ESMA, ECB and relevant central bank. Coming soon
Art. 20(5) EBA, ESMA and ECB issue non-binding opinions within 20 days, which authority must consider. Coming soon
Art. 21 Grant or refusal of the authorisation
Art. 21(1) Authority decides within 25 working days of opinions; authorisation approves the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 21(2) Authority must refuse authorisation on demonstrable grounds listed.
Art. 21(2)(a) Refusal ground: management body may threaten sound management or market integrity. Coming soon
Art. 21(2)(b) Refusal ground: managers fail the suitability criteria. Coming soon
Art. 21(2)(c) Refusal ground: qualifying shareholders fail the good repute criteria. Coming soon

Art. 21(4) Authority must refuse authorisation after a negative central bank opinion on payment risks. Coming soon

Art. 22 Reporting on asset-referenced tokens
Art. 22(1) Issuers of large tokens report quarterly to authority on holders, reserve and transactions.
Art. 22(1)(a) Quarterly report states number of holders. Coming soon
Art. 22(1)(b) Quarterly report states value issued and reserve size. Coming soon
Art. 22(1)(c) Quarterly report gives average daily transaction count and value. Coming soon
Art. 22(1)(d) Quarterly report estimates daily transactions used as payment within one currency area. Coming soon
Art. 22(2) Authority may extend reporting duty to smaller token issuances. Coming soon
Art. 22(3) Service providers must supply issuers the data needed for quarterly reports. Coming soon
Art. 22(4) Authority shares received reports with central banks and host-state authorities. Coming soon

Art. 22(7) EBA drafts standard forms and templates for reporting and data provision. Coming soon
Art. 23 Restrictions on the issuance of asset-referenced tokens used widely as a means of exchange
Art. 23(1) Widely used payment tokens above stated thresholds trigger issuer obligations.
Art. 23(1)(a) Issuer must stop issuing the token once thresholds are exceeded. Coming soon
Art. 23(1)(b) Issuer submits within 40 working days a plan to reduce usage below thresholds. Coming soon
Art. 23(2) Authority uses the highest available estimate to judge whether threshold is reached. Coming soon
Art. 23(3) Where multiple issuers issue one token, their data is aggregated. Coming soon
Art. 23(4) Authority approves the plan and may require modifications such as minimum denominations. Coming soon
Art. 23(5) Issuance may resume only with evidence usage is below thresholds. Coming soon
Art. 24 Withdrawal of the authorisation
Art. 24(1) Authorities must withdraw issuer authorisation in listed situations; issuer reports some.
Art. 24(1)(a) Withdrawal if issuer is inactive for six months or unused for twelve. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(b) Withdrawal if authorisation was obtained by irregular means such as false statements. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(c) Withdrawal if issuer no longer meets authorisation conditions. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(d) Withdrawal if issuer seriously breaches the Title's provisions. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(e) Withdrawal if issuer is subject to a redemption plan. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(f) Withdrawal if issuer renounces authorisation or decides to cease operations. Coming soon
Art. 24(1)(g) Withdrawal if activity seriously threatens market integrity, stability or invites laundering risks. Coming soon
Art. 24(2) Authority withdraws authorisation if central bank finds serious threat to payments or monetary policy. Coming soon
Art. 24(3) Authorities cap issuance or set a minimum denomination when central bank warns of systemic threat. Coming soon
Art. 24(4) Authorities must promptly tell the issuer's regulator about certain adverse situations.
Art. 24(4)(a) Notification when a third-party entity loses its credit, crypto, payment or e-money authorisation. Coming soon
Art. 24(4)(b) Notification when managers or qualifying shareholders breach anti-money-laundering law. Coming soon
Art. 24(5) Authorisation is withdrawn where repute or governance is compromised; issuer then follows redemption procedure. Coming soon
Art. 24(6) Authorities report a withdrawal to ESMA within two working days; ESMA records it. Coming soon
Art. 25 Modification of published crypto-asset white papers for asset-referenced tokens
Art. 25(1) Issuers notify the regulator 30 working days before significant business model changes.
Art. 25(1)(a) Changes to governance arrangements, reporting lines and risk management must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(b) Changes to reserve assets and their custody must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(c) Changes to token holders' rights must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(d) Changes to the issuance and redemption mechanism must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(e) Changes to transaction validation protocols must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(f) Changes to the issuer's own distributed ledger operation must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(g) Changes to liquidity mechanisms and liquidity management policy must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(h) Changes to third-party arrangements for reserve, custody and distribution must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(i) Changes to complaints-handling procedures must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(1)(j) Changes to money laundering risk assessment and related policies must be notified. Coming soon
Art. 25(2) Issuer drafts modified white paper in original order; authority acknowledges and decides within set deadlines. Coming soon
Art. 25(3) Authority consults central banks and optionally EBA/ESMA on modifications affecting payment systems or monetary policy. Coming soon
Art. 25(4) On approving a modified white paper, authority may impose corrective measures, including central bank proposals.
Art. 25(4)(a) Issuer may be required to add holder-protection mechanisms when operational changes materially affect token value. Coming soon
Art. 25(4)(b) Issuer may be required to take corrective measures on market integrity or payment systems. Coming soon
Art. 25(5) Authority forwards the modified white paper to EU bodies within two working days; ESMA registers it. Coming soon
Art. 26 Liability of issuers of asset-referenced tokens for the information given in a crypto-asset white paper
Art. 26(1) Issuer and its board are liable to holders for losses from misleading white paper information. Coming soon
Art. 26(2) Contract terms excluding or limiting that civil liability have no legal effect. Coming soon
Art. 26(3) Holder must prove the infringement and that reliance affected their decision. Coming soon
Art. 26(4) No liability from the summary alone, except in specified circumstances.
Art. 26(4)(a) Liability applies if the summary is misleading or inconsistent with the rest of the paper. Coming soon
Art. 26(4)(b) Liability applies if the summary omits key information for prospective holders. Coming soon
Art. 26(5) Other civil liability under national law is unaffected. Coming soon

Art. 27(1) Issuers act honestly, fairly, professionally and communicate clearly and non-misleadingly with holders. Coming soon
Art. 27(2) Issuers act in holders' best interests and treat them equally unless disclosed. Coming soon
Art. 28 Publication of the crypto-asset white paperIssuer publishes approved and modified white papers on its website, kept available while tokens are held. Coming soon
Art. 29 Marketing communications
Art. 29(1) Marketing communications must meet listed requirements.
Art. 29(1)(a) Marketing must be clearly identifiable as marketing. Coming soon
Art. 29(1)(b) Marketing information must be fair, clear and not misleading. Coming soon
Art. 29(1)(c) Marketing must be consistent with the white paper. Coming soon
Art. 29(1)(d) Marketing states the white paper exists and gives website, phone and email contacts. Coming soon

Art. 29(3) Marketing communications and changes must be published on the issuer's website. Coming soon

Art. 29(5) Marketing communications must be provided to authorities on request. Coming soon
Art. 29(6) No marketing before white paper publication, though market soundings are allowed. Coming soon

Art. 30(2) Issuers publish a summary and the full unredacted reserve audit report. Coming soon

Art. 31(3) Issuers provide a complaint template and keep records of complaints and responses. Coming soon

Art. 32(1)(b) Conflicts policy covers holders of qualifying shareholdings. Coming soon
Art. 32(1)(c) Conflicts policy covers management body members. Coming soon
Art. 32(1)(d) Conflicts policy covers employees. Coming soon
Art. 32(1)(e) Conflicts policy covers token holders. Coming soon
Art. 32(1)(f) Conflicts policy covers third parties performing outsourced functions. Coming soon
Art. 32(2) Particular care for conflicts arising from managing and investing the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 32(3) Issuers prominently disclose conflict sources and mitigation steps on their website. Coming soon
Art. 32(4) Conflict disclosure must be precise enough for informed purchasing decisions. Coming soon

Art. 32(5)(b) Standards specify disclosure content and methodology. Coming soon
Art. 33 Notification of changes to management bodyIssuers immediately notify the authority of management body changes with assessment information. Coming soon

Art. 34(1) Issuers need robust governance, clear responsibilities, risk processes and internal controls. Coming soon
Art. 34(2) Management body members must be of good repute, skilled, and have sufficient time. Coming soon
Art. 34(3) Management body periodically reviews effectiveness of compliance policies and fixes deficiencies. Coming soon
Art. 34(4) Qualifying shareholders must be of good repute without relevant convictions. Coming soon
Art. 34(5) Issuers adopt effective compliance policies, and third-party arrangements are set in contracts.
Art. 34(5)(a) Policies on the reserve of assets. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(b) Policies on reserve custody and asset segregation. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(c) Policies on rights granted to token holders. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(d) Policies on how tokens are issued and redeemed. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(e) Policies on transaction validation protocols. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(f) Policies on operation of the issuer's proprietary ledger technology. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(g) Policies on liquidity mechanisms and liquidity management. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(h) Policies on third-party arrangements for reserve operation, investment, custody and distribution. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(i) Policies on written consent for others offering or listing the token. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(j) Policies on complaints handling. Coming soon
Art. 34(5)(k) Policies on conflicts of interest. Coming soon
Art. 34(6) Issuers use adequate systems for continuity and keep security access protocols compliant with Union standards. Coming soon
Art. 34(7) Issuer submits a discontinuation plan to the authority for approval before ceasing services. Coming soon

Art. 34(13)(c) Guidelines cover the internal control mechanism. Coming soon

Art. 35 Own funds requirements
Art. 35(1) Issuers always hold own funds at least the highest of three measures.
Art. 35(1)(a) Own funds floor of EUR 350,000. Coming soon
Art. 35(1)(b) Own funds of at least two percent of average reserve assets. Coming soon
Art. 35(1)(c) Own funds of a quarter of prior-year fixed overheads. Coming soon
Art. 35(2) Own funds must consist of Common Equity Tier 1 items after deductions. Coming soon
Art. 35(3) Authority may require up to twenty percent more own funds when risk is higher.
Art. 35(3)(a) Risk indicator: quality of risk management and internal controls. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(b) Risk indicator: quality and volatility of the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(c) Risk indicator: types of rights granted to holders. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(d) Risk indicator: investment policy risks where the reserve is invested. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(e) Risk indicator: value and number of settled transactions. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(f) Risk indicator: importance of markets where the token is offered. Coming soon
Art. 35(3)(g) Risk indicator: market capitalisation of the token. Coming soon

Art. 35(6)(b) Standards on criteria for requiring higher own funds. Coming soon
Art. 35(6)(c) Standards on minimum design of stress testing programmes.
Art. 35(6)(c)(i) Stress test types, objectives and applications. Coming soon
Art. 35(6)(c)(ii) Frequency of stress testing exercises. Coming soon
Art. 35(6)(c)(iii) Internal governance arrangements for stress testing. Coming soon
Art. 35(6)(c)(iv) Relevant data infrastructure for stress testing. Coming soon

Art. 35(6)(c)(vi) Applying proportionality to the minimum stress test requirements. Coming soon

Art. 36 Obligation to have a reserve of assets, and composition and management of such reserve of assets
Art. 36(1) Issuers must constitute and always maintain a reserve of assets, composed and managed properly.
Art. 36(1)(a) Reserve must be managed so risks of the referenced assets are covered. Coming soon
Art. 36(1)(b) Reserve must address liquidity risks from holders' permanent redemption rights. Coming soon
Art. 36(2) Reserve must be legally separated from issuer's estate and other tokens' reserves, shielding from creditors. Coming soon
Art. 36(3) Reserve must be operationally separated from issuer's own estate and other tokens' reserves. Coming soon

Art. 36(4)(a) Standards set share of reserve maturing daily, including one-day-notice repos or cash. Coming soon
Art. 36(4)(b) Standards set share of reserve maturing weekly, including five-day-notice repos or cash. Coming soon
Art. 36(4)(c) Standards cover other maturities and general liquidity management techniques. Coming soon
Art. 36(4)(d) Standards set minimum bank deposits per currency, at least thirty percent. Coming soon
Art. 36(5) Each token needs its own separately managed reserve pool; shared tokens share one reserve. Coming soon
Art. 36(6) Management must run the reserve prudently; issuance and redemption must match reserve changes. Coming soon
Art. 36(7) Reserve valued at market prices must at least equal holders' claims on circulating tokens. Coming soon
Art. 36(8) Issuers need a clear, detailed policy describing the token's stabilisation mechanism.
Art. 36(8)(a) Policy lists the referenced assets and their composition. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(b) Policy describes reserve asset types and exact allocation. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(c) Policy includes detailed assessment of credit, market, concentration and liquidity risks of the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(d) Policy describes issuance and redemption procedure and its matching effect on the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(e) Policy states whether any reserve portion is invested under Article 38. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(f) If invested, policy details investment approach and its effect on reserve value. Coming soon
Art. 36(8)(g) Policy describes how tokens are bought and redeemed, and who may do so. Coming soon
Art. 36(9) Issuers must commission an independent reserve audit every six months. Coming soon
Art. 36(10) Audit results go to the authority within six weeks and are published within two weeks after.
Art. 36(10)(a) Authority may delay publication when a recovery arrangement was required. Coming soon
Art. 36(10)(b) Authority may delay publication when a redemption plan was required. Coming soon
Art. 36(10)(c) Authority may delay publication to protect holders' economic interests. Coming soon
Art. 36(10)(d) Authority may delay publication to avoid significant harm to the financial system. Coming soon
Art. 36(11) Reserve valued by mark-to-market at prudent bid/offer side, using good-quality market data.
Art. 36(11)(a) Data quality assessed by number and quality of counterparties. Coming soon
Art. 36(11)(b) Data quality assessed by market volume and turnover of the asset. Coming soon
Art. 36(11)(c) Data quality assessed by size of the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 36(12) If market pricing unavailable, value conservatively with a model, never amortised cost.
Art. 36(12)(a) Model must reflect market volume and turnover of the asset. Coming soon
Art. 36(12)(b) Model must reflect the size of the reserve. Coming soon
Art. 36(12)(c) Model must reflect market, interest rate and credit risk of the asset. Coming soon
Art. 37 Custody of reserve assets
Art. 37(1) Issuers must maintain custody policies and contracts ensuring reserve safeguards at all times.

Art. 37(1)(b) Reserve assets must be held in custody as paragraph 6 prescribes. Coming soon
Art. 37(1)(c) Issuers must have prompt access to reserve assets for redemption requests. Coming soon
Art. 37(1)(d) Concentration among custodians must be avoided. Coming soon

Art. 37(3) Reserve assets must be held by an eligible custodian within five working days of issuance.

Art. 37(3)(b) Any reserve asset type may be custodied by a credit institution. Coming soon
Art. 37(3)(c) Financial instrument reserves may be custodied by an investment firm offering safekeeping. Coming soon
Art. 37(4) Issuers must carefully select custodians, distinct from themselves, with contracts protecting assets from custodian creditors. Coming soon
Art. 37(5) Custody policies set custodian selection criteria; issuers regularly review custodians and monitor their finances. Coming soon
Art. 37(6) Custodians must hold reserve assets in segregated accounts named for the issuer, per reserve.
Art. 37(6)(a) Credit institutions hold funds in an account in their books. Coming soon
Art. 37(6)(b) Financial instruments are held in custody by credit institutions or investment firms, registered or physically delivered. Coming soon
Art. 37(6)(c) Crypto-asset providers hold the crypto-assets or their private access keys. Coming soon
Art. 37(6)(d) For other assets, credit institutions verify issuer ownership and keep records. Coming soon
Art. 37(7) Custodian appointment must be documented by contract regulating necessary information flow. Coming soon
Art. 37(8) Custodians must act honestly, fairly, professionally, independently, in interest of issuers and holders. Coming soon
Art. 37(9) Custodians must avoid conflicting activities with issuers unless safeguards are met.
Art. 37(9)(a) Custody tasks must be functionally and hierarchically separated from conflicting tasks. Coming soon
Art. 37(9)(b) Conflicts must be identified, monitored, managed and disclosed to holders. Coming soon
Art. 37(10) Custodian that loses an asset must promptly compensate the issuer, barring unavoidable external events. Coming soon

Art. 38(5)(d)(ii) Limit share of assets custodied with providers in the same group. Coming soon

Art. 39(2) Issuers redeem in funds or referenced assets, with a policy and same-currency redemption option.

Art. 39(2)(c) Policy sets valuation principles for tokens and reserve assets at redemption. Coming soon

Art. 43(2) EBA classifies a token as significant when at least three criteria are met.

Art. 51(1)(b) White paper includes information about the e-money token. Coming soon
Art. 51(1)(c) White paper includes information on the public offer or trading admission. Coming soon
Art. 51(1)(d) White paper includes rights and obligations attached to the token. Coming soon
Art. 51(1)(e) White paper includes information on underlying technology. Coming soon
Art. 51(1)(f) White paper includes information on risks. Coming soon

Art. 51(6)(b) Summary warns purchase decisions should rest on the whole white paper. Coming soon
Art. 51(6)(c) Summary warns the offer is not a solicitation to buy financial instruments. Coming soon

Art. 52(4)(b) Liability where summary lacks key information when read with the white paper. Coming soon

Art. 60(7) Lists the information that entities must include in their notification.

Art. 67(6)(g) Coverage for liability to clients under Article 75(8). Coming soon
Art. 68 Governance arrangements
Art. 68(1) Management body members need good repute, suitable skills, no relevant convictions, and enough time. Coming soon
Art. 68(2) Qualifying shareholders must be of good repute without relevant convictions. Coming soon
Art. 68(3) Authorities act where shareholder influence threatens sound and prudent management. Coming soon
Art. 68(4) Providers adopt policies and procedures effective for ensuring compliance with the Regulation. Coming soon

Art. 68(7) Ensure service continuity with resilient, secure ICT systems and a business continuity policy with recovery plans. Coming soon
Art. 68(8) Maintain anti-money-laundering systems and safeguard data availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality. We fix

arch.privileged-key-client-sideA privileged key shipped to browsers lets any user read and change all data, so data confidentiality and integrity are not safeguarded.

db.multi-write-no-txA change to several tables without a transaction can stop half-way and leave inconsistent data, so integrity is not safeguarded.

db.result-unchecked auto-fix: writes, in JavaScript and TypeScript with supabase-jsAn unread query error lets a failed write pass as success, losing data without notice.

db.rls-missingA table without row-level security lets every API role read and write all rows, against data confidentiality and integrity.

db.transition-unguardedA state change that does not check the current state lets concurrent requests apply conflicting transitions to orders or transfers.

db.version-uncheckedIgnoring the version column lets a stale write overwrite a newer one, corrupting records.

secrets.committedA credential readable by everyone with the repository leaves the data it guards without confidentiality.

secrets.in-historyA secret recoverable from git history and not rotated keeps the data it guards open to anyone with a clone.

tls.verification-disabledWithout certificate checks data in transit loses authenticity and confidentiality, which Art. 68(8) requires to be safeguarded.
Art. 68(9) Keep records of all services, orders and transactions for five to seven years. We detect

db.cascade-deletes-historyWhere the history is of crypto-asset services, orders or transactions, deleting a row erases records MiCA requires to keep for five years.

Art. 72(1)(a)(ii) Conflicts with persons linked to it or its owners by control. Coming soon

Art. 76(1)(b) Rules define categories of crypto-assets excluded from trading. Coming soon
Art. 76(1)(c) Rules state policies, procedures and any fees for admission to trading. Coming soon

Art. 88(4)(b) Standards cover delaying public disclosure of inside information. Coming soon

Art. 89(3)(b) No recommending or inducing cancelling or amending orders based on inside information. Coming soon

Art. 89(5)(b) Covers those holding capital in the issuer or offeror. Coming soon
Art. 89(5)(c) Covers those with access through employment, duties or role in distributed ledger technology. Coming soon

Art. 91(2)(a)(ii) Behaviour holding prices at an abnormal or artificial level. Coming soon

Art. 91(3)(b)(i) Disrupting or delaying the trading platform's functioning. Coming soon
Art. 91(3)(b)(ii) Making genuine orders harder to identify or destabilising the platform. Coming soon
Art. 91(3)(b)(iii) Entering orders creating false signals or starting or intensifying a trend. Coming soon
Art. 91(3)(c) Voicing opinions on a held asset and profiting without disclosing the conflict. Coming soon

Art. 103 ESMA temporary intervention powers
Art. 103(1) ESMA may temporarily prohibit or restrict certain crypto-asset activities under conditions.

Art. 103(1)(b) ESMA may restrict a type of activity or practice involving non-ART/EMT crypto-assets. Coming soon

Art. 103(2)(b) Existing Union requirements must not already address the threat. Coming soon
Art. 103(2)(c) A competent authority has failed to act adequately on the threat. Coming soon
Art. 103(3) ESMA's measure must avoid disproportionate harm and regulatory arbitrage.

Art. 103(3)(b) The measure must not create a risk of regulatory arbitrage. Coming soon

Art. 103(7) ESMA measures override earlier national authority measures on the same matter. Coming soon

Art. 104(3)(a) The measure must not harm market efficiency or holders disproportionately to its benefits. Coming soon
Art. 104(3)(b) The measure must not create a risk of regulatory arbitrage. Coming soon
Art. 104(4) EBA must notify relevant authorities before taking a measure. Coming soon
Art. 104(5) EBA publishes a notice of the measure with details and effective time. Coming soon

Art. 104(7) EBA measures override earlier national authority measures on the same matter. Coming soon

Art. 105(3)(c) Notification must include evidence showing the intervention conditions are met. Coming soon

Art. 105(5) Authority publishes a notice of the measure with details, start time and evidence. Coming soon
Art. 105(6) Authority must revoke a restriction once the conditions no longer apply. Coming soon
Art. 105(7) The Commission adopts delegated acts specifying criteria for authorities' threat assessment. Coming soon

Art. 111 Administrative penalties and other administrative measures
Art. 111(1) Member States give authorities power to impose administrative penalties for listed infringements, with notification duties.
Art. 111(1)(a) Penalties cover breaches of the rules on offers of other crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 111(1)(b) Penalties cover breaches of asset-referenced token issuer requirements. Coming soon
Art. 111(1)(c) Penalties cover breaches of e-money token requirements. Coming soon
Art. 111(1)(d) Penalties cover breaches of service provider authorisation and conduct requirements. Coming soon
Art. 111(1)(e) Penalties cover breaches of market abuse rules. Coming soon
Art. 111(1)(f) Penalties cover failure to cooperate with investigations, inspections or requests. Coming soon
Art. 111(2) Minimum penalty powers for the first four infringement groups.
Art. 111(2)(a) Authority can issue a public statement naming the responsible party and infringement. Coming soon
Art. 111(2)(b) Authority can order the offender to stop and not repeat the conduct. Coming soon
Art. 111(2)(c) Fines up to at least double the gains or avoided losses. Coming soon
Art. 111(2)(d) Natural persons face maximum fines of at least EUR 700,000. Coming soon
Art. 111(3) Minimum maximum fines for legal persons, using consolidated turnover for groups.
Art. 111(3)(a) Legal persons face fines of at least EUR 5 million for first four groups. Coming soon
Art. 111(3)(b) Fines of at least 3% of turnover for offer-rule breaches. Coming soon
Art. 111(3)(c) Fines of at least 5% of turnover for service provider breaches. Coming soon
Art. 111(3)(d) Fines of at least 12.5% of turnover for token issuer breaches. Coming soon
Art. 111(4) Authorities can temporarily bar responsible individuals from management roles in service providers. Coming soon
Art. 111(5) Minimum sanctions and measures for market abuse infringements, with consolidated turnover for groups.
Art. 111(5)(a) Public statement naming the responsible party and infringement. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(b) Order to cease the conduct and not repeat it. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(c) Disgorgement of profits gained or losses avoided where determinable. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(d) Withdrawal or suspension of a service provider's authorisation. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(e) Temporary management ban for responsible individuals in service providers. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(f) Management ban of at least ten years for repeated market abuse breaches. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(g) Temporary ban on responsible individuals trading on their own account. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(h) Fines up to at least triple the profits gained or losses avoided. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(i) Minimum fine ceilings for natural persons: EUR 1 million or EUR 5 million by article. Coming soon
Art. 111(5)(j) Minimum fine ceilings for legal persons, in euros or turnover percentage. Coming soon
Art. 111(6) Member States may grant extra powers and set higher penalties. Coming soon
Art. 112 Exercise of supervisory powers and powers to impose penalties
Art. 112(1) Authorities weigh all relevant circumstances when choosing penalty type and level.
Art. 112(1)(a) Consider seriousness and length of the infringement. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(b) Consider whether the breach was deliberate or careless. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(c) Consider how responsible the offender is. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(d) Consider the offender's financial resources, via turnover or income and assets. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(e) Consider the scale of profits gained or losses avoided. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(f) Consider losses caused to third parties. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(g) Consider the offender's cooperation with the authority. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(h) Consider earlier infringements of the Regulation by the offender. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(i) Consider steps the offender took to avoid recurrence. Coming soon
Art. 112(1)(j) Consider the effect on holders and clients, especially retail ones. Coming soon
Art. 112(2) Authorities cooperate and coordinate to avoid overlap in cross-border enforcement. Coming soon
