Art. 123(1)(e) Investigators may request telephone and data traffic records. Coming soon
Art. 123(2) Investigators act on written authorisation stating subject, purpose and applicable penalties and fines. Coming soon
Art. 123(3) Issuers must submit to investigations ordered by EBA decision, which states scope, penalties and remedies. Coming soon
Art. 123(4) EBA notifies the host State authority beforehand, which assists and may attend. Coming soon
Art. 123(5) EBA applies for court authorisation where national law requires it for traffic records. Coming soon
Art. 123(6) A court asked to authorise traffic record requests checks the decision.
Art. 123(6)(a) Court verifies EBA's decision is authentic. Coming soon
Art. 123(6)(b) Court verifies measures are proportionate, not arbitrary or excessive. Coming soon
Art. 123(7) Court may seek explanations from EBA but cannot review necessity; only the Court of Justice reviews lawfulness. Coming soon
Art. 124 On-site inspections
Art. 124(1) EBA may conduct on-site inspections at issuers' premises and must inform the college of relevant findings. Coming soon
Art. 124(2) Inspectors may enter premises, use investigative powers, and seal premises and records as needed. Coming soon
Art. 124(3) EBA gives the host authority notice of inspections, and may inspect unannounced where needed. Coming soon
Art. 124(4) Inspectors act on written authorisation stating subject, purpose and penalties for non-submission. Coming soon
Art. 124(5) Issuers must submit to inspections ordered by EBA decision, which sets start date and remedies. Coming soon
Art. 124(6) Host State authority officials must assist EBA inspectors on request and may attend. Coming soon
Art. 124(7) EBA may require national authorities to carry out investigations and inspections on its behalf. Coming soon
Art. 124(8) Host authority must give inspectors needed help, including police, if someone opposes an inspection. Coming soon
Art. 124(9) EBA applies for court authorisation where national law requires it for inspections. Coming soon
Art. 124(10) A court asked to authorise an inspection or assistance checks the decision.
Art. 124(10)(a) Court verifies EBA's decision is authentic. Coming soon
Art. 124(10)(b) Court verifies measures are proportionate, not arbitrary or excessive. Coming soon
Art. 124(11) Court may seek explanations from EBA but cannot review necessity; only the Court of Justice reviews lawfulness. Coming soon
Art. 125 Exchange of information
Art. 125(1) EBA and national authorities must exchange information needed for their duties without undue delay.
Art. 125(1)(a) Exchanged information covers significant asset-referenced token issuers and their controlling or controlled entities. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(b) Authorities may exchange information with contracted third parties of significant asset-referenced token issuers. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(c) Information exchange extends to custodians of reserve assets, whether service providers, credit institutions or investment firms. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(d) Information exchange covers significant e-money token issuers and entities controlling or controlled by them. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(e) Information exchange covers payment service providers handling payments for significant e-money tokens. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(f) Information exchange covers persons distributing significant e-money tokens for the issuer. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(g) Information exchange covers custody providers holding significant tokens on behalf of clients. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(h) Information exchange covers trading platforms admitting significant asset-referenced or e-money tokens. Coming soon
Art. 125(1)(i) Information exchange also covers the management bodies of all the listed persons. Coming soon
Art. 125(2) Authorities may refuse exchange or investigation cooperation requests only in listed circumstances.
Art. 125(2)(a) Refusal permitted if complying would likely harm the authority's own investigations or enforcement. Coming soon
Art. 125(2)(b) Refusal permitted if court proceedings already started on same actions and persons. Coming soon
Art. 125(2)(c) Refusal permitted if a final judgment already exists for same actions and persons. Coming soon
Art. 126 Administrative agreements on the exchange of information between EBA and third countries
Art. 126(1) EBA may agree information exchange with third-country supervisors only with equivalent professional secrecy guarantees. Coming soon
Art. 126(2) Exchanged information must serve the tasks of EBA or the foreign supervisor. Coming soon
Art. 126(3) EBA applies Regulation 2018/1725 when transferring personal data to third countries. Coming soon
Art. 127 Disclosure of information from third countries
Art. 127(1) EBA may disclose third-country information only with the sending authority's express consent or for judicial proceedings. Coming soon
Art. 127(2) Express consent is not needed for other EU supervisors or courts in criminal matters. Coming soon
Art. 128 Cooperation with other authoritiesEBA cooperates with authorities supervising an issuer's other, non-MiCA activities, including tax authorities. Coming soon
Art. 129 Professional secrecyProfessional secrecy binds EBA, its current and former staff, and delegates such as auditors. Coming soon
Art. 130 Supervisory measures by EBA
Art. 130(1) EBA may take listed measures when a significant asset-referenced token issuer infringes Annex V.
Art. 130(1)(a) EBA can order the token issuer to stop the infringing conduct. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(b) EBA can impose fines or periodic penalty payments. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(c) EBA can require extra information to protect token holders, especially retail holders. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(d) EBA can suspend a public offer for up to 30 working days. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(e) EBA can prohibit a public offer of the token when infringement is found or suspected. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(f) EBA can require a trading platform to suspend trading for up to 30 working days. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(g) EBA can prohibit trading of the token on a platform after an infringement. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(h) EBA can require marketing communications to be amended if they breach Article 29. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(i) EBA can suspend or prohibit marketing communications on suspected infringement. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(j) EBA can require disclosure of all material information affecting assessment of the token. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(k) EBA can issue warnings that the issuer fails its obligations. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(l) EBA can withdraw the issuer's authorisation. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(m) EBA can require removal of a person from the issuer's management body. Coming soon
Art. 130(1)(n) EBA can require a minimum denomination or a cap on the amount issued. Coming soon
Art. 130(2) EBA may take listed measures when a significant e-money token issuer infringes Annex VI.
Art. 130(2)(a) EBA can order the e-money token issuer to stop the infringing conduct. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(b) EBA can impose fines or periodic penalty payments. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(c) EBA can require supplementary information to protect e-money token holders. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(d) EBA can suspend a public offer for up to 30 working days. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(e) EBA can prohibit a public offer of the e-money token on infringement or suspicion. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(f) EBA can require a trading platform to suspend e-money token trading for up to 30 working days. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(g) EBA can prohibit trading of significant e-money tokens on a platform after infringement. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(h) EBA can require disclosure of all material information affecting assessment of the e-money token. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(i) EBA can issue warnings that the issuer fails its obligations. Coming soon
Art. 130(2)(j) EBA can require a minimum denomination or limit on issuance of the e-money token. Coming soon
Art. 130(3) EBA must weigh the nature and seriousness of the infringement when choosing measures.
Art. 130(3)(a) Factor: how long and how often the infringement occurred. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(b) Factor: whether financial crime was caused or facilitated by the infringement. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(c) Factor: whether it exposed serious or systemic weaknesses in procedures, policies or risk management. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(d) Factor: whether the infringement was intentional or negligent. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(e) Factor: the issuer's degree of responsibility. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(f) Factor: the issuer's financial strength, shown by turnover or income and assets. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(g) Factor: the impact on token holders' interests. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(h) Factor: profits gained, losses avoided or third-party losses, where determinable. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(i) Factor: the issuer's level of cooperation with EBA. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(j) Factor: the issuer's previous infringements. Coming soon
Art. 130(3)(k) Factor: steps the issuer took afterwards to prevent repetition. Coming soon
Art. 130(4) Before certain asset-referenced token measures, EBA informs ESMA and relevant central banks. Coming soon
Art. 130(5) Before e-money token measures, EBA informs the issuer's competent authority and the relevant central bank. Coming soon
Art. 130(6) EBA notifies measures promptly and publishes decisions within 10 working days, without personal data. Coming soon
Art. 130(7) Public disclosure of decisions must include statements about appeal rights.
Art. 130(7)(a) Disclosure must state the right to appeal to the Court of Justice. Coming soon
Art. 130(7)(b) Where relevant, disclosure must state an appeal was lodged and has no suspensive effect. Coming soon
Art. 130(7)(c) Disclosure must state the Board of Appeal may suspend the contested decision. Coming soon
Art. 131 Fines
Art. 131(1) EBA must fine issuers or management members who intentionally or negligently commit infringements.
Art. 131(1)(a) Fine applies to significant asset-referenced token issuers infringing Annex V. Coming soon
Art. 131(1)(b) Fine applies to significant e-money token issuers infringing Annex VI. Coming soon
Art. 131(2) When fining, EBA weighs the nature and seriousness of the infringement.
Art. 131(2)(a) Factor: duration and frequency of the infringement. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(b) Factor: whether financial crime was facilitated by the infringement. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(c) Factor: serious or systemic weaknesses in the issuer's procedures and risk management. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(d) Factor: intentional versus negligent commission. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(e) Factor: the issuer's degree of responsibility. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(f) Factor: issuer's financial strength by turnover or income and net assets. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(g) Factor: impact on holders' interests. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(h) Factor: profits gained, losses avoided or losses to third parties. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(i) Factor: the issuer's cooperation with EBA. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(j) Factor: earlier infringements by the issuer. Coming soon
Art. 131(2)(k) Factor: post-infringement measures to prevent recurrence. Coming soon
Art. 131(3) Fines on asset-referenced token issuers are capped at 12.5% of turnover or twice the gain. Coming soon
Art. 131(4) Fines on e-money token issuers are capped at 10% of turnover or twice the gain. Coming soon
Art. 132 Periodic penalty payments
Art. 132(1) EBA imposes periodic penalty payments to compel compliance in listed situations.
Art. 132(1)(a) Penalty payments can compel a person to stop infringing conduct per an EBA decision. Coming soon
Art. 132(1)(b) Penalty payments can compel persons referred to in Article 122(1).
Art. 132(1)(b)(i) Compel provision of complete information requested by decision. Coming soon
Art. 132(1)(b)(ii) Compel submission to investigation, including producing complete records and correcting information. Coming soon
Art. 132(1)(b)(iii) Compel submission to an ordered on-site inspection. Coming soon
Art. 132(2) Periodic penalties must be effective, proportionate and charged per day of delay. Coming soon
Art. 132(3) Daily penalty is 3% of average daily turnover, or 2% of income for individuals. Coming soon
Art. 132(4) Penalty runs at most six months, then EBA reviews it. Coming soon
Art. 133 Disclosure, nature, enforcement and allocation of fines and periodic penalty payments
Art. 133(1) EBA publicly discloses every fine and penalty payment, barring stability risk or disproportionate harm. Coming soon
Art. 133(2) Fines and periodic penalty payments are administrative in nature. Coming soon
Art. 133(3) Fines are enforced under civil procedure rules of the enforcing State. Coming soon
Art. 133(4) Collected fines and penalties go to the Union's general budget. Coming soon
Art. 133(5) If EBA declines to fine, it informs EU institutions and authorities with reasons. Coming soon
Art. 134 Procedural rules for taking supervisory measures and imposing fines
Art. 134(1) EBA appoints an independent investigation officer when infringement is clearly suspected. Coming soon
Art. 134(2) Investigation officer investigates, considers comments, and submits a complete findings file to EBA. Coming soon
Art. 134(3) Investigation officer may use information, investigation and inspection powers, complying with Article 121. Coming soon
Art. 134(4) Investigation officer has access to all documents EBA gathered while supervising. Coming soon
Art. 134(5) Persons investigated must be heard before findings are submitted; findings rely only on commented facts. Coming soon
Art. 134(6) Defence rights of persons concerned must be fully respected. Coming soon
Art. 134(7) Investigated persons are notified of submission and may access the file, protecting business secrets. Coming soon
Art. 134(8) EBA decides on infringement from the file and takes measures or fines. Coming soon
Art. 134(9) Investigation officer stays out of EBA's deliberations and decision-making. Coming soon
Art. 134(10) Commission adopts delegated acts on procedural rules for fines by 30 June 2024. Coming soon
Art. 134(11) EBA refers possible criminal matters to national authorities and avoids fines after res judicata. Coming soon
Art. 135 Hearing of the persons concerned
Art. 135(1) Before decisions, EBA lets investigated persons comment and relies only on commented findings. Coming soon
Art. 135(2) Hearing can be deferred for urgent action, with an interim decision and later hearing. Coming soon
Art. 135(3) Defence rights are respected, with file access subject to business secrets and confidentiality. Coming soon
Art. 136 Review by the Court of JusticeThe Court of Justice has unlimited jurisdiction to review EBA fines and penalties. Coming soon
Art. 137 Supervisory fees
Art. 137(1) EBA charges supervisory fees to significant token issuers to cover its costs. Coming soon
Art. 137(2) Fee scales with reserve asset size or e-money issuance volume. Coming soon
Art. 137(3) Commission adopts a delegated act on fee types, amounts and payment by 30 June 2024. Coming soon
Art. 138 Delegation of tasks by EBA to competent authorities
Art. 138(1) EBA may delegate specific supervisory tasks to a competent authority when necessary. Coming soon
Art. 138(2) EBA consults the competent authority before delegating a task.
Art. 138(2)(a) Consultation covers the scope of the delegated task. Coming soon
Art. 138(2)(b) Consultation covers the timetable for the task. Coming soon
Art. 138(2)(c) Consultation covers information transmission to and from EBA. Coming soon
Art. 138(3) EBA reimburses competent authorities for costs of delegated tasks per the fees act. Coming soon
Art. 138(4) EBA reviews delegations periodically and may revoke them at any time. Coming soon
Art. 139 Exercise of the delegation
Art. 139(1) Commission's power to adopt delegated acts is subject to this Article's conditions. Coming soon
Art. 139(2) Delegation lasts 36 months from mid-2023, with Commission report and tacit renewal. Coming soon
Art. 139(3) Parliament or Council may revoke the delegation at any time without affecting existing acts. Coming soon
Art. 139(4) Commission must consult Member State experts before adopting a delegated act. Coming soon
Art. 139(5) Commission notifies Parliament and Council simultaneously when adopting a delegated act. Coming soon
Art. 139(6) Delegated acts take effect only absent objection within three months, extendable by three more. Coming soon
Art. 140 Reports on the application of this Regulation
Art. 140(1) Commission reports on the Regulation's application by mid-2027, with interim report in 2025. Coming soon
Art. 140(2) Introduces the list of required contents for the Commission's reports.
Art. 140(2)(a) Report covers issuance counts, white papers submitted, asset types, market capitalisation and trading admissions. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(b) Report describes experience classifying crypto-assets and divergent approaches among authorities. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(c) Report assesses whether white papers for other tokens need an approval mechanism. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(d) Report estimates Union residents using or investing in Union-issued crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(e) Report estimates residents holding non-Union crypto-assets, and explains data availability. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(f) Report gives figures on fraud, hacks, thefts, ransomware payments and complaints. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(g) Report covers asset-referenced token issuers, reserve categories and size, and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(h) Report covers significant asset-referenced token issuers, their reserves and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(i) Report covers e-money token issuers, referenced currencies, funds held and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(j) Report covers significant e-money token issuers, currencies, reserves and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(k) Report states the number of significant crypto-asset service providers. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(l) Report assesses crypto-asset market functioning, trends, authorised providers and market shares. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(m) Report assesses protection level for holders and clients, especially retail. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(n) Report assesses fraudulent marketing and scams on social media involving crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(o) Report assesses issuer and provider requirements' impact on resilience, integrity, stability and protection. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(p) Report evaluates Article 81 and possible appropriateness tests in Articles 78 to 80. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(q) Report assesses whether service scope, definitions and new crypto-asset forms need adjusting. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(r) Report assesses whether provider prudential requirements should align with investment firm rules. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(s) Report assesses significance thresholds for asset-referenced and e-money tokens and periodic review. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(t) Report assesses decentralised finance development and appropriate regulatory treatment. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(u) Report assesses thresholds for significant service providers and whether to review them periodically. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(v) Report assesses whether to create an equivalence regime for third-country entities. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(w) Report assesses whether the exemptions in Articles 4 and 16 are appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(x) Report assesses internal market impact, including SME financing and new payment means. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(y) Report covers business and technology developments, environmental impact and mitigation options. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(z) Report appraises whether changes are needed to protect clients, market integrity and stability. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(aa) Report covers application of administrative penalties and other measures. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(ab) Report evaluates cooperation among authorities and weighs national versus EBA supervision. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(ac) Report evaluates authority–ESMA cooperation and weighs who should supervise significant providers. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(ad) Report states compliance costs for other-token issuers as share of funds raised. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(ae) Report states compliance costs for token issuers as share of operational costs. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(af) Report states service providers' compliance costs as share of operational costs. Coming soon
Art. 140(2)(ag) Report gives number and amount of fines and criminal penalties imposed. Coming soon
Art. 140(3) Reports must also follow up on topics from the Article 141 and 142 reports. Coming soon
Art. 141 ESMA annual report on market developmentsESMA publishes an annual market-developments report, with authorities supplying needed information.
Art. 141(a) ESMA report covers issuances, white papers, asset types, capitalisation and trading admissions. Coming soon
Art. 141(b) ESMA report covers asset-referenced token issuers, reserves and transaction volumes. Coming soon
Art. 141(c) ESMA report covers significant asset-referenced token issuers, reserves and transaction volumes. Coming soon
Art. 141(d) ESMA report covers e-money token issuers, currencies, funds and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 141(e) ESMA report covers significant e-money token issuers, currencies, reserves and payment volumes. Coming soon
Art. 141(f) ESMA report counts crypto-asset service providers and significant ones. Coming soon
Art. 141(g) ESMA report estimates Union residents using or investing in Union-issued crypto-assets. Coming soon
Art. 141(h) ESMA report estimates residents holding non-Union crypto-assets where possible, noting data availability. Coming soon
Art. 141(i) ESMA report maps unauthorised exchanges serving Union residents, their location and customer-checking levels. Coming soon
Art. 141(j) ESMA report gives share and volume of transactions via providers versus peer-to-peer. Coming soon
Art. 141(k) ESMA report gives figures on fraud, hacks, thefts, ransomware payments and complaints. Coming soon
Art. 141(l) ESMA report counts complaints about false or misleading white papers and marketing. Coming soon
Art. 141(m) ESMA report proposes ways to reduce circumvention, including unauthorised third-country service provision. Coming soon
Art. 142 Report on latest developments in crypto-assets
Art. 142(1) Commission reports by end-2024 on latest crypto-asset developments, including unaddressed matters. Coming soon
Art. 142(2) Introduces minimum contents of the Commission's developments report.
Art. 142(2)(a) Report assesses decentralised finance and the need and feasibility of regulating it. Coming soon
Art. 142(2)(b) Report assesses need and feasibility of regulating crypto-asset lending and borrowing. Coming soon
Art. 142(2)(c) Report assesses treatment of e-money token transfer services not covered by payment review. Coming soon
Art. 142(2)(d) Report assesses non-fungible crypto-asset markets and the feasibility of regulating them. Coming soon
Art. 143 Transitional measures
Art. 143(1) Articles 4 to 15 do not apply to public offers ended before December 2024. Coming soon
Art. 143(2) Limits which Title II rules apply to crypto-assets admitted to trading before December 2024.
Art. 143(2)(a) Marketing communication rules in Articles 7 and 9 apply to post-2024 publications. Coming soon
Art. 143(2)(b) Trading platform operators must ensure a white paper exists for legacy assets by end-2027. Coming soon
Art. 143(3) Existing providers may continue until July 2026 or authorisation decision; Member States may shorten. Coming soon
Art. 143(4) Existing non-bank asset-referenced token issuers continue pending authorisation if they apply by July 2024. Coming soon
Art. 143(5) Credit institutions issuing asset-referenced tokens continue pending white paper approval if they notify by July 2024. Coming soon
Art. 143(6) Member States may use a simplified authorisation procedure for already nationally authorised providers. Coming soon
Art. 143(7) EBA exercises supervisory duties once the delegated acts on significance apply. Coming soon
Art. 144 Amendment to Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010Amends the scope clause of the EBA founding Regulation to include this Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 145 Amendment to Regulation (EU) No 1095/2010Amends the scope clause of the ESMA founding Regulation to include this Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 146 Amendment to Directive 2013/36/EUReplaces a point in Annex I of the Capital Requirements Directive.
Art. 146(15) Adds issuing e-money, including e-money tokens, to the activities list in the banking directive. Coming soon
Art. 146(16) Adds asset-referenced token issuance to the credit institution activities list. Coming soon
Art. 146(17) Adds crypto-asset services to the credit institution activities list. Coming soon
Art. 147 Amendment to Directive (EU) 2019/1937Adds a point to the whistleblower directive's annex.
Art. 147(xxii) Adds this crypto-assets regulation to the whistleblower directive's list of protected reporting areas. Coming soon
Art. 148 Transposition of amendments to Directives 2013/36/EU and (EU) 2019/1937
Art. 148(1) Member States adopt laws implementing the directive amendments by end of 2024. Coming soon
Art. 148(2) Member States send national measures on Article 116 matters to Commission, EBA and ESMA. Coming soon
Art. 149 Entry into force and application
Art. 149(1) Regulation enters into force twenty days after Official Journal publication. Coming soon
Art. 149(2) Regulation generally applies from 30 December 2024. Coming soon
Art. 149(3) Titles III and IV apply earlier, from 30 June 2024. Coming soon
Art. 149(4) Listed empowering provisions and Article 139 apply from June 2023; Regulation is directly applicable. Coming soon
Annex I DISCLOSURE ITEMS FOR THE CRYPTO-ASSET WHITE PAPER FOR CRYPTO-ASSETS OTHER THAN ASSET-REFERENCED TOKENS OR E-MONEY TOKENS
Annex I Part A Information about the offeror or the person seeking admission to tradingWhite paper must include information about the offeror or person seeking admission.
Annex I Part A 1 White paper states the offeror's name. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 2 White paper states the offeror's legal form. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 3 White paper gives registered address and head office if different. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 4 White paper gives the offeror's registration date. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 5 White paper gives a legal entity identifier or national equivalent. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 6 White paper gives contact phone and email plus promised response time. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 7 White paper names the parent company where applicable. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 8 White paper identifies management body members with addresses and roles. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 9 White paper describes the offeror's and parent's business or professional activity. Coming soon
Annex I Part A 10 White paper reviews the offeror's three-year financial condition and performance. Coming soon
Annex I Part B Information about the issuer, if different from the offeror or person seeking admission to tradingWhite paper must include information about the issuer when it differs from the offeror.
Annex I Part B 1 White paper states the issuer's name. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 2 White paper states the issuer's legal form. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 3 White paper gives the issuer's registered address and head office if different. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 4 White paper gives the issuer's registration date. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 5 White paper gives the issuer's legal entity identifier or national equivalent. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 6 White paper names the issuer's parent company where applicable. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 7 White paper identifies the issuer's management body members, addresses and functions. Coming soon
Annex I Part B 8 White paper describes the issuer's and parent's business or professional activity. Coming soon
Annex I Part C Information about the operator of the trading platform in cases where it draws up the crypto-asset white paperWhite paper must include platform operator information when the operator drafts it.
Annex I Part C 1 White paper states the platform operator's name. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 2 White paper states the platform operator's legal form. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 3 White paper gives the operator's registered address and head office if different. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 4 White paper gives the operator's registration date. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 5 White paper gives the operator's legal entity identifier or national equivalent. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 6 White paper names the operator's parent company where applicable. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 7 White paper explains why the operator drew up the white paper. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 8 White paper identifies the operator's management body members, addresses and functions. Coming soon
Annex I Part C 9 White paper describes the operator's and parent's business or professional activity. Coming soon
Annex I Part D Information about the crypto-asset projectWhite paper must include information about the crypto-asset project.
Annex I Part D 1 White paper gives project and asset names and ticker abbreviation. Coming soon
Annex I Part D 2 White paper briefly describes the crypto-asset project. Coming soon
Annex I Part D 3 White paper details all persons involved in implementing the project, with addresses. Coming soon
Annex I Part D 4 For utility tokens, white paper states key features of goods or services planned. Coming soon
Annex I Part D 5 White paper gives project milestones and resources already allocated. Coming soon
Annex I Part D 6 White paper states planned use of any funds or crypto-assets collected. Coming soon
Annex I Part E Information about the offer to the public of crypto-assets or their admission to tradingWhite paper section disclosing details of the public offer or admission to trading.
Annex I Part E 1 State whether the white paper covers a public offer or trading admission. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 2 Explain why the offer or trading admission is being pursued. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 3 Disclose fundraising target, subscription limits, and handling of oversubscription. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 4 Give the issue price, subscription fees, or how price is determined. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 5 Give total quantity of crypto-assets offered or admitted, where relevant. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 6 Identify targeted prospective holders and any limits on holder types. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 7 Notify purchasers of refund rights and describe the refund mechanism and timeline. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 8 Describe offer phases, early-buyer discounts, reasons for price differences and impact on others. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 9 State the subscription period for offers that are time-limited. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 10 Describe how funds or assets are safeguarded during the offer and withdrawal period. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 11 Describe payment methods and how value is returned when refunds are due. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 12 Provide information on purchasers' withdrawal right under Article 13. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 13 Explain how and when purchased crypto-assets are delivered to holders. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 14 State technical requirements a purchaser must meet to hold the assets. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 15 Name any placing service provider and whether placement is firm commitment. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 16 Name the target trading platform, access method and costs. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 17 Disclose the expenses of the public offer. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 18 Disclose potential conflicts of interest among those involved in the offer. Coming soon
Annex I Part E 19 State governing law and competent court for the offer. Coming soon
Annex I Part F Information about the crypto-assetsWhite paper section describing the crypto-assets offered.
Annex I Part F 1 State the type of crypto-asset offered or sought for trading. Coming soon
Annex I Part F 2 Describe asset characteristics, register classification data, functionality and rollout timing. Coming soon
Annex I Part G Information on the rights and obligations attached to the crypto-assetsWhite paper section on rights and obligations attached to the crypto-assets.
Annex I Part G 1 Describe purchaser rights and obligations and how to exercise them. Coming soon
Annex I Part G 2 Describe when rights and obligations may be changed. Coming soon
Annex I Part G 3 Disclose planned future offers and amount of assets the issuer retains. Coming soon

Annex I Part G 5 For utility tokens, explain how they are redeemed for goods or services. Coming soon
Annex I Part G 6 If not admitted to trading, say how and where assets can be traded afterwards. Coming soon

Annex I Part G 9 Describe value-protection and compensation schemes, where they exist. Coming soon

Annex I Part H 1 Describe the ledger technology, protocols and technical standards used. Coming soon
Annex I Part H 2 Describe the consensus mechanism where one applies. Coming soon

Annex VI 1 Issuers of large non-EU-currency e-money tokens must report quarterly information to EBA. Coming soon

Reuse: Official EU legislation on EUR-Lex, free to read; reuse terms in the EUR-Lex legal notice (not re-checked); cite article numbers and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
